published_prior_art.cite: Joo2025 supplies an MVN minimax rule and plug-in asymptotics; GuggenbergerHuang2025 supplies convergence for a discretized game, neither a continuous-cell outward certificate with all-minimizer enclosure.
AronowGreenLee2014 gives two-margin sharp variance bounds, not a shared three-slice binary full-tie covariance realization.
HiranoPorter2009 transfers smooth local experiments; LiuHudgens2014 and JiangImaiMalani2023 give fixed-mechanism randomization results, not the stated pilot-selected, changing-face transfer.
HiranoPorter2009 already gives local-minimax lower-bound machinery; the proposed zero-information boundary application is setting-specific.
VanderWeeleTchetgen2011 distinguishes type-A/type-B mechanisms but does not give the exact-hit Gaussian regret ratio or equality criterion.
This is a useful worked numerical consequence of the exact-hit result, rather than an independently broad theorem.

soundness_flags.label: ass:local-covariance-neighborhood
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited HiranoPorter2009 local-experiment condition is a DQM/local-path condition, not the proposal's shrinking sup-norm covariance-neighborhood condition with sqrt(C)d_C→∞; retag it novel and justify it, or cite a source establishing this exact uniform condition.

soundness_flags.label: def:finite-population-class; thm:attainable-binary-box; oeq:uniform-primitive-risk-sandwich
soundness_flags.one_line: “Calibrated covariance,” its diagonal Gaussian representation, the observed statistic/selector k-hat, and the map from finite-population local arrays to h and r are not defined, so the asserted primitive risk inequalities have no determinate experiment or quantifier domain.

soundness_flags.label: ass:active-local-tie; oeq:uniform-primitive-risk-sandwich
soundness_flags.one_line: The class requires active welfare gaps o(C^{-1/2}), while the OEQ lower bound ranges over nonzero and expanding local h directions; define a baseline-plus-local-array family with U_C,i-U_C,j=(h_i-h_j)/sqrt(C)+o(C^{-1/2}) and state which members belong to the supremum.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 7, Theorem 2.3; p. 9, Proposition 3.2; p. 12, Theorem 4.2
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 2.3 gives the deterministic unique MMR strategy, Proposition 3.2 gives continuity in covariance on a compact positive-definite set, and Theorem 4.2 gives plug-in asymptotic attainment under LUCLT.
Proposition 1 states convergence of Algorithm 1's maximal regret to the minimax value of the epsilon-discretized model.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 5–6, Section 3.1 and Proposition 3.1; pp. 12–13, Theorem 3.5 and Section 4.1
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper localizes around g(theta_0)=0 through theta_0+h/sqrt(n), imposes DQM/nonsingular information, and states local-minimax comparisons over h; it does not state the proposal's shrinking covariance-neighborhood condition.

source_verification_receipts.locator: issue metadata and article abstract; publisher full theorem text inaccessible
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The published article exists at the cited venue and pages and concerns randomized-saturation designs, standard errors, and optimal-design insights. The exact theorem-number wording in the comparator table requires checking against the publisher PDF before use as a load-bearing comparison.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define the finite-population observation vector, the estimator/selector k-hat, the calibrated covariance functional including cross-coordinate covariances, and the exact relation between a design sequence and r.
Replace the single o(C^{-1/2}) tie condition by a formally defined baseline-plus-local perturbation family indexed by h, then restate both sides of the risk sandwich over that same family.
Retag or properly source the covariance-neighborhood condition, and obtain the published Baird PDF to verify the comparator-table theorem references before retaining them.

Add a complete three-policy, full-tie worked receipt from primitives; the current two-policy numerical calculation is a valuable unit test but does not exhibit the full certificate claimed by the kernel.
